payload.title: Prenup Requirements in Australia and Who Needs One
payload.excerpt: In Australia, a prenup is a binding financial agreement, a contract made under Part VIIIA of the Family Law Act 1975 for married couples.
key_takeaways: Legal Aid NSW says an agreement can protect an inheritance a partner may receive in future, or property for children from a previous relationship.
Legal Aid NSW says an agreement made overseas is not automatically recognised in Australia and must meet the formal requirements to be valid here.
The Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia says the agreement binds only if it meets the Act's technical requirements, including independent legal advice for each partner before signing.
A court can set an agreement aside in some circumstances, and Legal Aid NSW lists fraud among its grounds.

faq.q: Are prenups legally binding in Australia?
faq.a: Yes, if the agreement meets the technical requirements of section 90G of the Family Law Act, according to the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia. Once made it is legally enforceable, and Legal Aid NSW says a court can set it aside only in limited circumstances.

faq.q: What is a prenup called in Australia?
faq.a: A binding financial agreement, or financial agreement, made under Part VIIIA of the Family Law Act 1975 for married couples.

faq.q: How long does a prenup last in Australia?
faq.a: Until it is ended or set aside. Victoria Legal Aid says that to change or end an agreement, both parties must get legal advice again and sign a new written agreement, called a termination agreement. Legal Aid NSW says it can be changed or ended by a new agreement with a terminating clause, a termination agreement, or abandonment.

faq.q: Can you do your own prenup without a lawyer?
faq.a: No. The Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia says you cannot enter into a financial agreement without each first getting independent legal advice from an Australian lawyer.

faq.q: What happens to a prenup if one partner dies?
faq.a: Legal Aid NSW says the agreement stays in force even if one party dies, unless it specifically says otherwise.

faq.q: Can we sign a prenup after the wedding?
faq.a: Yes. An agreement can be made during the marriage or after it.
